curriculum.lesson_evidence: Viewpoint is the height of your eye compared with the object you are drawing. From up high, looking down, a mug’s opening is a wider ellipse and you see more of the inside. From a lower seat, looking slightly up, that ellipse flattens, less inside shows, more of the base appears, and the mug looks taller against its opening.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
You already drew a cup while looking down, with a wide opening. What should change in a second drawing made from a lower angle?

FEEDBACK
The opening ellipse should flatten, less of the inside should show, and the cup should look taller. More of the lower edge or underside can appear. Stay in the lower seat for the whole drawing so the ellipse does not change halfway. The cup itself did not grow; your eye moved.

WATCH FOR
Changing where you sit changes nothing in the drawing, because a mug is the same object and must always have the same ellipse.

INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
From a lower seat, Eli sees a flatter opening ellipse and a taller-looking mug. His first drawing, made looking down, had a wide ellipse and a visible inside. He then sits so his eyes are nearer the table height: the opening closes toward a thinner ellipse, the inside almost disappears, and the lower edge becomes clearer. He does not mix the wide top with the low base in one drawing.

TRY FIRST
You already drew a cup while looking down, with a wide opening. What should change in a second drawing made from a lower angle?

FEEDBACK
The opening ellipse should flatten, less of the inside should show, and the cup should look taller. More of the lower edge or underside can appear. Stay in the lower seat for the whole drawing so the ellipse does not change halfway. The cup itself did not grow; your eye moved.
teach_steps.explain:
Viewpoint is the height of your eye compared with the object you are drawing. From up high, looking down, a mug’s opening is a wider ellipse and you see more of the inside. From a lower seat, looking slightly up, that ellipse flattens, less inside shows, more of the base appears, and the mug looks taller against its opening.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the elements, techniques or performance choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For movement or instruments, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby and stop if anything feels unsafe. You may always describe a choice instead of performing it. One deliberate artistic choice with a named effect is more useful than a longer praise sentence.
